items.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: I got Eddie Jones in the band, Bill Hughes, Sonny Cohn, Eric Dixon, Thad Jones, I can’t think, oh Al Aarons.

ctx.x: What was it like playing in different parts of the world with the Basie band?

Oh, we always had a good following. And the band was hot. We were in one of the best bands Basie ever had. And that’s the band that made him rich, you know. The band was tight. I had forgotten actually, how good the band was until I was listening to those Mosaic recordings. And then it came back to me, how good that band was. It was like one person playing, you know. Everybody was—it was a good band. Well Basie, he knew how to do that. You know he didn’t fault nobody. He just let it stay there until the cats got…
Were you happy switching from the tenor to the alto?

items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: He recorded with Frank Wess in 1952, then joined Basie for the first time in 1954

ctx.x: have become standards. Frank is now devoting his time to performing with small groups and composing new music. He was recently honored at a Town Hall Celebration in New York City.

Bill Hughes has been a familiar face in the Basie trombone section for many years. Born in Dallas, Texas, his first band experience was with Andy Kirk. He recorded with Frank Wess in 1952, then joined Basie for the first time in 1954, staying until ‘57. His recorded solo on “Magic” is a trademark and since 1964, Bill has been a presence with the Basie Orchestra, currently holding down the bass trombone chair.
Bill and Frank were interviewed together following a concert in Schenectady, New York on March 28, 1995, by Michael Woods and Monk Rowe.
